So IT personnel are no longer an option in the modern business world, the only question that businesses have is whether to in-source or out-source their IT services. This means that employment in IT services can be broadly broken down into two categories: in house, and contractor. This is the same framework that many skilled trades have followed for a long time. Which side of that divide you are on is going to make a huge difference in what your job is going to be like.

Contracting/consulting is generally: higher paying, faster paced, and more stressful. This is because your time and effort is being sold to companies as a product. It can further be subdivided into independent consulting, and employment with a consulting firm. Independent consulting takes everything to the max, you are responsible for everything: finding clients, booking time, quotes, billing. It's daunting, but the lean business model can reap huge profits. Working for a firm means they handle all the back end work for you, but they take their cut and expect you to produce.

In-house work varies widely from organization to organization and can broadly be broken down by size class. Small organizations expect their IT personnel to be one man operations. You will be expected to be a jack of all but a master of no disciplines. If you have a problem or project that you can't handle, you'll generally hire one of the aforementioned consultants to come in and assist. Medium sized organizations need advanced services enough that they start hiring specialists. They usually will have one or two specialists in any number of fields they need, that are expected to work as a team and have enough general IT knowledge to cover any skills gaps. Expect to have to be in a general on call rotation at this level.

Large organizations have enough need of IT services that they create entire teams of specialists. You will have teams for: desktop support, AD/Exchange, Networking, Security, etc. Within these organizations you will be a real specialist. You will wind up mastering one discipline. You can usually sit in these position and cruise for a long time, or buckle down and go full nerd and learn enough to springboard you into a better job. You should expect to be in an on call rotation within your specialty at this level.
